mos-bias-atlas.title: Bias
mos-bias-atlas.prompt: With 5 V, k = 2 mA/V², $V_T$ = 1 V, $R_D$ = 1 kΩ and $V_G$ = 2 V, find the bias. Ignore lambda.
mos-bias-atlas.hint: Try saturation and then test $V_{DS}$ ≥ u.

solution.text: Saturation needs $V_{DS}\ge u$: 4 V ≥ 1 V, with 3 V of margin.

mos-bias-atlas.title: Boundary
mos-bias-atlas.prompt: For the same device with $R_D$ = 2 kΩ, find the maximum gate voltage that still gives saturation.
mos-bias-atlas.hint: Set the drain voltage equal to overdrive.

solution.step: Express V_D in terms of u
solution.text: With k = 2 mA/V², $I_D=u^2$ (mA with u in volts), and $R_D$ = 2 kΩ.
The source is grounded, so the boundary is $V_D=u$.

mos-bias-atlas.title: Feedback
mos-bias-atlas.prompt: At $I_D$ = 1 mA and $g_m$ = 2 mS, compare a source resistor of 0 and 500 Ω with $R_D$ = 2 kΩ. Treat these as independently established bias points with infinite $r_o$ and no body effect.
mos-bias-atlas.hint: Use the incremental source feedback factor.

solution.answer: −4 and −2 V/V; the gate bias must rise by 0.5 V to keep 1 mA with $R_S$.

mos-diode-load.title: Resistance
mos-diode-load.prompt: A diode-connected MOSFET has $g_m$ = 1 mS and $g_{ds}$ = 10 μS. Find its incremental resistance.

solution.text: With gate tied to drain, a test voltage $v$ drives current through both $g_m$ (since $v_{gs}=v$) and $g_{ds}$.

solution.answer: About 990 Ω, close to $1/g_m$, not the 100 kΩ $r_o$.

mos-diode-load.title: Size
mos-diode-load.prompt: A 1 mA stage has $k_n$ = 2 mA/V² and $k_L$ = 0.5 mA/V². With both thresholds 1 V and $V_{DD}$ = 5 V, find input and output voltages.

solution.text: The diode-connected load sits between $V_{DD}$ and the output.
Input device: $V_{DS}$ = 2 V ≥ 1 V. The load is diode-connected, so always saturated.

mos-diode-load.title: Gain
mos-diode-load.prompt: Use $g_{mn}$ = 2 mS, $g_{mL}$ = 1 mS, $g_{dsn}$ = $g_{dsL}$ = 20 μS and an AC-coupled 10 kΩ output load. Find gain.
mos-diode-load.hint: Keep the load conductance in the output KCL equation.

solution.text: The input device drives $-g_{mn}v_{in}$ into the node; the load conductances are the diode load's $g_{mL}$, both $g_{ds}$ and the 10 kΩ load.

mos-current-mirror.title: Reference
mos-current-mirror.prompt: For $I_{REF}$ = 0.25 mA, k = 2 mA/V² and $V_T$ = 1 V, find gate voltage and ideal compliance.

solution.text: The output device stays saturated while $V_{DS}\ge u$.

mos-current-mirror.title: Mismatch
mos-current-mirror.prompt: At 0.5 V overdrive, estimate the relative current error from a +5 mV threshold shift.

mos-current-mirror.title: Output Slope
mos-current-mirror.prompt: A device has $I_0$ = 1 mA and lambda = 0.02 V⁻¹. How much does its current rise when $V_{DS}$ changes by 2 V?
mos-current-mirror.hint: Differentiate the modulation factor at fixed gate voltage.

mos-ratioed-mirrors.title: Polarity
mos-ratioed-mirrors.prompt: A 5 V PMOS source has overdrive 0.4 V. What is the highest output voltage allowing saturation?
mos-ratioed-mirrors.hint: Subtract overdrive from the source rail.

solution.text: A PMOS stays saturated while $V_{SD}\ge u$.

mos-ratioed-mirrors.title: Ratio
mos-ratioed-mirrors.prompt: A 100 μA reference feeds mirror ratios 1, 2 and 5. Find the total DC supply current, including the reference branch.

solution.text: The reference itself also draws 100 µA from the supply.

mos-ratioed-mirrors.title: Degeneration
mos-ratioed-mirrors.prompt: A 1:4 mirror uses 1 kΩ in the 0.25 mA reference source. Choose the output source resistor for a 1 mA target.

solution.text: Equal gate voltages and equal $V_{GS}$ (the 4× device carries 4× current at the same overdrive) need equal source drops.
Resistors scale inversely with the current ratio: 1 kΩ/4.

mos-source-degeneration.title: Gain
mos-source-degeneration.prompt: At $g_m$ = 2 mS, $r_o$ = 50 kΩ, $R_D$ = 5 kΩ and $R_S$ = 500 Ω, calculate gain with no body effect.

mos-source-degeneration.title: Resistance
mos-source-degeneration.prompt: For the same transistor and source resistor, find current-source output resistance.
mos-source-degeneration.hint: Use a drain test current with the gate AC grounded.

mos-source-degeneration.title: Headroom
mos-source-degeneration.prompt: A 1 mA current sink has $R_S$ = 500 Ω and overdrive 0.5 V. Find minimum output voltage.
mos-source-degeneration.hint: Add source drop to channel compliance.

solution.text: Saturation needs $V_{DS}\ge u$ = 0.5 V.

mos-cascode-mirror.title: Resistance
mos-cascode-mirror.prompt: Find cascode resistance for $g_m=1$ mS and both $r_o=100$ kΩ.

solution.answer: 10.2 MΩ; 0.5 V moves the current by about 49 nA.

mos-cascode-mirror.title: Headroom
mos-cascode-mirror.prompt: Use $V_T=0.7$ V and $u=0.3$ V. Find standard output compliance and upper gate bias.

solution.text: In the standard cascode mirror the lower drain sits at $V_{GS}$.

mos-cascode-mirror.title: Mismatch
mos-cascode-mirror.prompt: A lower output device has a 5 mV threshold increase at $u=0.5$ V. Estimate current error.

solution.text: The cascode raises output resistance but copies whatever current the lower device sets, so it does not correct mismatch.

mos-wide-swing-mirror.title: Bias
mos-wide-swing-mirror.prompt: For $u_1=0.2$ V, $u_2=0.3$ V, $V_{T2}=0.8$ V and margin 0.1 V, find $V_X,V_B,V_{out,min}$.

solution.text: Set it just enough above $u_1$, with margin.

mos-wide-swing-mirror.title: Replica
mos-wide-swing-mirror.prompt: An output device has $k=8$ mA/V² at 0.5 mA. What replica k doubles its overdrive?

solution.text: $u\propto1/\sqrt{k}$, so doubling u needs k divided by 4.

mos-wide-swing-mirror.title: Budget
mos-wide-swing-mirror.prompt: A 1.8 V supply must support a 1.5 V bias node and a 0.4 V reference-generator compliance. Is it feasible?

solution.text: The bias node and the generator's compliance stack in series.
The output stack alone fitting is not enough; every branch must fit.

mos-common-source.title: Gain
mos-common-source.prompt: Find gain for $g_m=3$ mS, $R_D=4$ kΩ and $r_o=40$ kΩ.

mos-common-source.title: Distortion
mos-common-source.prompt: Estimate second harmonic for 20 mV peak input at 0.4 V overdrive.

solution.text: For $v_{gs}=a\cos\omega t$, $H_2/H_1=a/(4u)$.

mos-common-source.title: Loading
mos-common-source.prompt: At gain −10, with $C_{gs}=8$ pF and $C_{gd}=1$ pF, estimate input capacitance and its pole with 50 kΩ source resistance.

solution.text: The drain moves −10 times the gate, so $C_{gd}$ sees 11 times the gate swing.

mos-active-load.title: Gain
mos-active-load.prompt: For $g_m=1$ mS and both output resistances 100 kΩ, find unloaded gain and gain with 50 kΩ AC load.

mos-active-load.title: Bias
mos-active-load.prompt: A 30 kΩ node experiences 15 μA current imbalance. Estimate the DC shift.

solution.step: Imbalance flows into the node resistance
solution.text: Any difference between the source and sink currents must flow through the node's small-signal resistance.

solution.answer: About 0.45 V; check that both devices stay saturated.

mos-active-load.title: Pole
mos-active-load.prompt: A 40 kΩ node has 20 pF capacitance. Find its pole.

mos-source-follower.title: Gain
mos-source-follower.prompt: Use $g_m=2$ mS, $g_{mb}=0.4$ mS, $g_{ds}=0.02$ mS and $R_L=10$ kΩ. Find gain.

solution.text: The gate drives $g_m$; body effect, $g_{ds}$ and the load all load the source.

solution.answer: Gain 0.794; output resistance 413 Ω (397 Ω with the load).

mos-source-follower.title: Dc
mos-source-follower.prompt: With no body effect, $V_G=3$ V, $V_T=1$ V, $k=2$ mA/V² and $R_L=2$ kΩ, solve source voltage.

solution.text: $V_S=I_DR_L$ and $I_D=\tfrac12k(V_G-V_T-V_S)^2$.
The '+' root (3.28 V) gives negative overdrive. Keep the other.

mos-source-follower.title: Transient
mos-source-follower.prompt: A 2 kΩ load discharges 1 nF from 2 V with the transistor off. Find initial slope and time constant.
mos-source-follower.hint: Use resistor current and capacitor charge.

mos-current-loaded-follower.title: Headroom
mos-current-loaded-follower.prompt: An NMOS follower has $u=0.4$ V above a sink with $u=0.2$ V on a 3 V supply. Find its ideal output interval.

solution.text: The sink needs $V_{DS}\ge u$ = 0.2 V.
The follower's drain is at 3 V; it needs $V_{DS}\ge$ 0.4 V.

mos-current-loaded-follower.title: Slew
mos-current-loaded-follower.prompt: A 200 μA sink discharges 2 nF with no other load. Find falling slope.

mos-current-loaded-follower.title: Power
mos-current-loaded-follower.prompt: A 0.8 mA unloaded path runs from a 5 V rail to ground. Find idle power.

solution.text: The current flows from 5 V to ground through both devices.

solution.answer: 4 mW, shared between follower and sink.

mos-common-gate.title: Ports
mos-common-gate.prompt: For $g_m=2$ mS, $g_{ds}=20$ μS and $R_D=10$ kΩ, find gain and input resistance.

solution.text: Drive the source with $v_s$, gate grounded. Both $g_m$ and $g_{ds}$ push current into $R_D$; $g_{ds}R_D$ appears in the denominator.
Without $r_o$: gain 20, input 500 Ω.

mos-common-gate.title: Generator
mos-common-gate.prompt: Use the previous stage with a 2 kΩ generator resistance. Find overall voltage gain.

mos-common-gate.title: Body
mos-common-gate.prompt: With $g_m=1$ mS, $g_{mb}=0.2$ mS and infinite output resistance, find input resistance.

solution.text: Both the gate and body are at AC ground, so the source sees $g_m+g_{mb}$.

mos-cascode-amplifier.title: Loading
mos-cascode-amplifier.prompt: Use stack $R_c=2$ MΩ, $G_m=1$ mS and active-load resistance 100 kΩ. Find gain.

mos-cascode-amplifier.title: Bias
mos-cascode-amplifier.prompt: A lower device needs 0.3 V overdrive with 0.1 V margin. Upper threshold is 0.8 V and overdrive 0.4 V. Find gate bias and minimum output.

mos-cascode-amplifier.title: Pole
mos-cascode-amplifier.prompt: A loaded node has 80 kΩ resistance and 5 pF capacitance. Find its isolated pole.

mos-differential-pair.title: Balance
mos-differential-pair.prompt: For $I_T=0.8$ mA and $k=5$ mA/V², find balanced overdrive and transconductance.
mos-differential-pair.hint: Each branch carries half the tail.

mos-differential-pair.title: Gain
mos-differential-pair.prompt: Use $g_{m0}=2$ mS and equal 4 kΩ drain loads. Find right-drain and differential gain.

solution.text: With $v_d=V_1-V_2$, the right gate moves by $-v_d/2$.
Its current falls by $g_mv_d/2$, so its drain rises.

mos-differential-pair.title: Steering
mos-differential-pair.prompt: For $I_T=1$ mA and $k=8$ mA/V², find the ideal full-steering threshold.

solution.text: All the tail flows in one device when the other's overdrive reaches zero.

mos-differential-range.title: Range
mos-differential-range.prompt: Use $V_{DD}=3.3$ V, $I_T=1$ mA, $R_D=2$ kΩ, $V_T=0.7$ V, $u_0=0.3$ V and $u_T=0.2$ V. Find balanced common-mode bounds.

solution.text: The tail needs $u_T$, and each input device needs $V_T+u_0$ above the tail node.
Saturation holds while the gate is no more than $V_T$ above the drain.

mos-differential-range.title: Rejection
mos-differential-range.prompt: For $g_m=1$ mS and $r_T=100$ kΩ, estimate single-ended CMRR.
mos-differential-range.hint: Use the factor of two in differential gain.

mos-differential-range.title: Linearity
mos-differential-range.prompt: For $u_0=0.2$ V, estimate the 1% gain-compression differential range.

solution.text: For the square-law pair, the effective gain falls as $\sqrt{1-v_d^2/(4u_0^2)}$.

mos-mirror-loaded-differential.title: Gain
mos-mirror-loaded-differential.prompt: For $g_m=1.5$ mS and both output resistances 80 kΩ, find differential single-ended gain.
mos-mirror-loaded-differential.hint: Combine the two current changes first.

solution.text: The mirror copies the left device's current change to the output, adding it to the right device's opposite change.

mos-mirror-loaded-differential.title: Swing
mos-mirror-loaded-differential.prompt: Let $V_S=0.4$ V, $u_N=0.3$ V, $V_{DD}=3.3$ V and $u_P=0.4$ V. Find output interval.

solution.text: The NMOS input device needs $V_{DS}\ge u_N$ above its source.
The PMOS mirror output needs $V_{SD}\ge u_P$.
A 1.8 V operating point permits about ±1.1 V.

mos-mirror-loaded-differential.title: Error
mos-mirror-loaded-differential.prompt: A 10 μA DC imbalance enters a 40 kΩ output node. Find local shift.

solution.text: A larger imbalance pushes a device out of saturation, so feedback must set the DC point.

mos-differential-degeneration.title: Gain
mos-differential-degeneration.prompt: For $g_m=4$ mS and $R_S=250$ Ω, find differential transconductance and drain-difference gain with 2 kΩ loads.

mos-differential-degeneration.title: Headroom
mos-differential-degeneration.prompt: Use $I_T=1$ mA, $R_S=1$ kΩ, $V_T=0.7$ V, $u_0=0.2$ V and $u_T=0.15$ V. Find lower common mode.
mos-differential-degeneration.hint: Each resistor carries half the tail.

mos-differential-degeneration.title: Steering
mos-differential-degeneration.prompt: For $I_T=1$ mA, $k=8$ mA/V² and $R_S=500$ Ω, find full-steering input.
mos-differential-degeneration.hint: Add resistor voltage at full imbalance.

solution.text: All 1 mA flows through one 500 Ω resistor.

mos-complementary-output.title: Bias
mos-complementary-output.prompt: For matched devices with $V_T=0.8$ V, $k=10$ mA/V² and $I_Q=0.2$ mA, find gate spread.

mos-complementary-output.title: Drive
mos-complementary-output.prompt: An upper NMOS must source 5 mA with $k=40$ mA/V² and $V_T=1$ V at output 3 V. Find gate voltage if the lower device is off.

mos-complementary-output.title: Power
mos-complementary-output.prompt: A complementary stage has ±12 V rails and 3 mA idle current. Find total idle power.

mos-two-stage-amplifier.title: Gain
mos-two-stage-amplifier.prompt: Stages have transconductances 0.8 and 3 mS, and resistances 80 and 40 kΩ. Find DC gain magnitude.

mos-two-stage-amplifier.title: Compensation
mos-two-stage-amplifier.prompt: For $g_{m1}=0.5$ mS and desired $f_u=2$ MHz, estimate Miller capacitance.

solution.text: With Miller compensation, $f_u=g_{m1}/(2\pi C_C)$.

mos-two-stage-amplifier.title: Slew
mos-two-stage-amplifier.prompt: A 40 pF capacitor can receive 80 μA. Find slew and maximum 1 V peak sine frequency before slew limiting.

solution.answer: 2 V/µs; 1 V peak up to 318 kHz.

mos-noise-design.title: Efficiency
mos-noise-design.prompt: For 0.25 V strong-inversion overdrive, find $g_m/I_D$ and current needed for 2 mS.

mos-noise-design.title: Noise
mos-noise-design.prompt: Combine 4 nV/√Hz amplifier noise with 12 nV/√Hz resistor noise.

mos-noise-design.title: Bandwidth
mos-noise-design.prompt: A first-order low-pass has 1 kHz −3 dB frequency and white input density 10 nV/√Hz. Find integrated rms input noise.
mos-noise-design.hint: Its equivalent noise bandwidth is $\pi f_c/2$.

opamp-ideal.title: Finite Gain
opamp-ideal.prompt: A noninverting gain-20 circuit has $A_0=20000$. Find its exact DC gain.

solution.text: For a noninverting stage the noise gain equals the ideal gain: 20.

opamp-ideal.title: Virtual Ground
opamp-ideal.prompt: An inverting stage has 0.8 V output and $A_0=80000$, with plus input at zero. Find minus-input voltage.

solution.answer: −10 µV: near ground, not exactly ground.

opamp-ideal.title: Limit
opamp-ideal.prompt: A gain-5 circuit has a 3 V positive output limit. What ideal input reaches it?

solution.answer: 0.6 V; leave margin below the swing limit.

opamp-dc-errors.title: Offset
opamp-dc-errors.prompt: A gain-25 amplifier has 80 μV offset. Find output offset before other errors.
opamp-dc-errors.hint: Offset is amplified by noise gain.

solution.step: Offset is referred to the input
solution.text: It appears in series with the noninverting input, so it is amplified by the noise gain.

opamp-dc-errors.title: Bias
opamp-dc-errors.prompt: With $R_F=90$ kΩ and $R_G=10$ kΩ, choose matching source resistance. If offset current is 4 nA, find residual output bias error.
opamp-dc-errors.hint: Use parallel resistance and noise gain.

solution.text: Put 9 kΩ in the noninverting path so equal bias currents create equal drops that cancel.
What remains is the offset current times 9 kΩ, times the noise gain of 10.

solution.answer: 9 kΩ; residual ≈ 360 µV at the output.

opamp-dc-errors.title: Drift
opamp-dc-errors.prompt: Offset drift is 0.5 μV/°C over 80°C, at noise gain 50. Find output drift contribution.
opamp-dc-errors.hint: Convert to equivalent input drift first.

opamp-ac-limits.title: Bandwidth
opamp-ac-limits.prompt: A 3 MHz single-pole op amp has inverting gain −9. Estimate bandwidth.

solution.text: For a single-pole op amp, closed-loop bandwidth ≈ $f_t/NG$.

opamp-ac-limits.title: Slew
opamp-ac-limits.prompt: Find required slew for a 3 V peak, 20 kHz sine.

opamp-ac-limits.title: Settling
opamp-ac-limits.prompt: A one-pole closed loop has 50 kHz bandwidth. Estimate 0.1% settling.

opamp-bjt-internals.title: Input
opamp-bjt-internals.prompt: At 25 μA collector current and $\beta=250$, find transconductance and base current at 300 K.

opamp-bjt-internals.title: Source
opamp-bjt-internals.prompt: A 100 nA input bias current flows through 200 kΩ. Find voltage error and output error at gain 5.
opamp-bjt-internals.hint: Ohm’s law followed by noise gain.

solution.text: Balance the resistance at the other input, or use a lower-bias-current amplifier.

solution.answer: 20 mV at the input, about 100 mV at the output.

opamp-bjt-internals.title: Steering
opamp-bjt-internals.prompt: For 100 μA tail and 10 mV differential input at 300 K, find current difference.

opamp-cmos-internals.title: Gm
opamp-cmos-internals.prompt: A MOS input branch runs at 20 μA and 0.16 V overdrive. Find transconductance.

opamp-cmos-internals.title: Range
opamp-cmos-internals.prompt: For threshold 0.6 V, input overdrive 0.15 V and tail overdrive 0.1 V, find the lower NMOS common-mode bound.

solution.text: It needs at least its overdrive, 0.1 V, across it.
Its gate must sit $V_T+u$ above the tail node.

solution.answer: About 0.85 V above the lower rail.

opamp-cmos-internals.title: Leakage
opamp-cmos-internals.prompt: Total leakage is 20 pA into a 5 MΩ source. Find input error.

solution.text: Include board and protection-diode leakage, not just the op amp.

solution.answer: 100 µV at the input, 2 mV at noise gain 20.

opamp-input-tradeoffs.title: Crossover
opamp-input-tradeoffs.prompt: An amplifier has 3 nV/√Hz voltage noise and 0.5 pA/√Hz current noise. Where are their contributions equal?

solution.text: Current noise flowing in source resistance R gives $i_nR$.

opamp-input-tradeoffs.title: Noise
opamp-input-tradeoffs.prompt: At 300 K, combine 5 nV/√Hz voltage noise, 0.2 pA/√Hz current noise and 100 kΩ source resistance.

solution.answer: About 45.6 nV/√Hz, dominated by the resistor.

opamp-input-tradeoffs.title: Dc
opamp-input-tradeoffs.prompt: A 50 pA bias current flows through 2 MΩ, while offset is 30 μV. Find worst-case input bound.
opamp-input-tradeoffs.hint: Add magnitudes for an uncorrelated guarantee.

solution.text: For a guarantee, add magnitudes.
Nominal signed terms might partly cancel, but that cannot be relied on.

opamp-noninverting.title: Current
opamp-noninverting.prompt: A 2 V output drives 500 Ω and a 100 kΩ/10 kΩ divider. Find required output current.

opamp-noninverting.title: Noise
opamp-noninverting.prompt: Find divider input-referred resistor noise at 300 K for $R_F=30$ kΩ and $R_G=10$ kΩ.

solution.text: Both resistors' noise reaches the inverting input through their parallel combination.

opamp-inverting-summing.title: Weights
opamp-inverting-summing.prompt: With $R_F=30$ kΩ, $R_1=10$ kΩ and $R_2=15$ kΩ, find weights and noise gain.
opamp-inverting-summing.hint: Apply KCL and then zero sources.

solution.text: Zero the sources: $R_1\parallel R_2$ = 6 kΩ.

opamp-inverting-summing.title: Reference
opamp-inverting-summing.prompt: For those resistors, use $V_R=0.5$ V, $V_1=0.2$ V and $V_2=0.3$ V. Find output.

solution.text: A voltage on the noninverting input is amplified by the noise gain.

opamp-inverting-summing.title: Speed
opamp-inverting-summing.prompt: An inverting gain −0.1 stage uses a 2 MHz one-pole op amp. Estimate bandwidth.
opamp-inverting-summing.hint: Signal gain is not noise gain.

solution.answer: About 1.8 MHz, set by noise gain, not signal gain.

opamp-difference.title: Exact
opamp-difference.prompt: For $a=2$ and $b=2.02$, find $c$ and common-mode gain.

solution.text: With inverting ratio a and noninverting divider ratio b:

opamp-difference.title: Error
opamp-difference.prompt: Use that circuit at 3 V common mode and zero differential input. Find output.

solution.text: Both inputs at 3 V.

opamp-difference.title: Matching
opamp-difference.prompt: What relative ratio mismatch gives approximately 80 dB resistor-limited CMRR at unity gain?
opamp-difference.hint: Convert dB to a voltage ratio.

opamp-instrumentation.title: Gain
opamp-instrumentation.prompt: For $R=12$ kΩ and $R_G=1$ kΩ with final gain 2, find total gain.

opamp-instrumentation.title: Range
opamp-instrumentation.prompt: At $V_C=2$ V, $G_1=20$ and $v_d=0.1$ V, find internal outputs.

solution.answer: 1 V and 3 V; check each amplifier's swing.

opamp-instrumentation.title: Offset
opamp-instrumentation.prompt: Two input bias returns are 1 MΩ and 1.1 MΩ with equal 5 nA currents. Find differential drop.

opamp-transimpedance.title: Range
opamp-transimpedance.prompt: Use $R_F=200$ kΩ and allowable output magnitude 4 V. Find current range.

opamp-transimpedance.title: Compensation
opamp-transimpedance.prompt: For $R_F=2$ MΩ, $C_{IN}=20$ pF and $f_t=2$ MHz, estimate starting $C_F$.

solution.text: Place the feedback zero near the geometric mean of $1/(2\pi R_FC_{IN})$ and $f_t$.

solution.answer: About 0.9 pF, comparable to stray capacitance.

opamp-transimpedance.title: Noise
opamp-transimpedance.prompt: Find thermal current-noise density of 1 MΩ at 300 K.

opamp-integrator.title: Ramp
opamp-integrator.prompt: For 20 kΩ input resistance, 5 nF feedback capacitance and 50 mV input, find initial slope.

opamp-integrator.title: Charge
opamp-integrator.prompt: A charge pulse of 2 nC reaches a 1 nF feedback capacitor. Find output change.

solution.text: The virtual ground forces all input charge onto the feedback capacitor.

opamp-integrator.title: Leak
opamp-integrator.prompt: With 2 MΩ parallel resistance and 20 nF capacitance, find leakage corner and retained fraction after 10 ms.

opamp-differentiator.title: Scale
opamp-differentiator.prompt: For $R_F=50$ kΩ and $C_{IN}=2$ nF, find output for a slow 2000 V/s ramp.

opamp-differentiator.title: Corner
opamp-differentiator.prompt: For $R_{IN}=20$ kΩ and $C_{IN}=1$ nF, find input-series corner.

opamp-differentiator.title: Response
opamp-differentiator.prompt: Both denominator corners are 10 kHz. At 10 kHz, how does exact magnitude compare with the derivative-only estimate?

solution.text: Each denominator factor is $1+j$, with magnitude $\sqrt2$ and angle 45°.
The magnitude is half the derivative-only value, and the two poles add −90° of phase.

solution.answer: Half the derivative estimate, with an extra −90°.

opamp-active-filters.title: Design
opamp-active-filters.prompt: Choose equal-RC 1 kHz natural frequency with 10 nF capacitors. Find R and Butterworth K.
opamp-active-filters.hint: Use the natural-frequency and Q formulas.

solution.text: Equal-RC Sallen–Key has $Q=1/(3-K)$. Set Q = 0.7071.
For example 16 kΩ, and a gain of 1.586 from $R_F/R_G$ = 0.586; recompute the response.

opamp-active-filters.title: Q
opamp-active-filters.prompt: Equal RC with K = 2.2 has what Q and natural-frequency gain relative to DC?

solution.step: Gain at f₀ relative to DC

opamp-active-filters.title: Sensitivity
opamp-active-filters.prompt: At K = 2.8, estimate fractional Q change for a +0.01 gain error.

opamp-precision-rectifier.title: Swing
opamp-precision-rectifier.prompt: An amplifier can reach 3.8 V and its diode drops 0.5 V. Find approximate positive measured-output limit.
opamp-precision-rectifier.hint: Check the node before the diode.

solution.text: The op-amp output can reach 3.8 V.
The diode drop rises with load current, so leave margin.

opamp-precision-rectifier.title: Droop
opamp-precision-rectifier.prompt: A 20 nF peak capacitor has 5 nA total leakage. Find loss over 50 ms.

opamp-precision-rectifier.title: Acquisition
opamp-precision-rectifier.prompt: Charge 10 nF by 2 V in 20 μs. Find average current.

opamp-current-servo.title: Design
opamp-current-servo.prompt: Set 20 mA using 0.4 V command. Find sense resistance and power.

opamp-current-servo.title: Error
opamp-current-servo.prompt: A 200 μV offset appears with 0.2 V command. Find fractional current error.

solution.text: The loop forces the sense voltage to the command plus the offset.

opamp-current-servo.title: Thermal
opamp-current-servo.prompt: A 24 V supply drives 50 mA through a load dropping 8 V and a sense resistor dropping 1 V. Find MOS power.

opamp-load-stability.title: Pole
opamp-load-stability.prompt: Use 40 Ω effective output resistance and 5 nF load. Find initial pole estimate.

opamp-load-stability.title: Drop
opamp-load-stability.prompt: A locally sensed output drives 4 mA through 47 Ω isolation. Find load voltage loss.

solution.text: Feedback is taken before the isolation resistor, so the loop cannot see this drop.

opamp-load-stability.title: Charge
opamp-load-stability.prompt: A 2 nF load must change by 3 V in 2 μs. Find average required current.

opamp-function-design.title: Log Ratio
opamp-function-design.prompt: At 300 K and $n=1$, find output change for a current ratio of 1000.

opamp-function-design.title: Oscillator
opamp-function-design.prompt: Design equal-RC Wien natural frequency 2 kHz with 5 nF capacitors. Find R.

solution.answer: About 15.9 kΩ; needs gain slightly above 3 plus amplitude control.

opamp-function-design.title: Chain
opamp-function-design.prompt: A ±2 mV sensor must produce ±0.8 V variation around a reference. Find gain and output error from 20 μV input offset.
opamp-function-design.hint: Scale signal and offset with the same total gain.

solution.answer: Gain 400; offset contributes 8 mV (1% of full scale).
